name: writing a verification and validation specification
from: Verification as folklore: checks that exist but cite no requirement, green runs read as proof of correctness, and coverage gaps known to individuals and recorded nowhere.
to: An ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-shaped register: every case naming the requirement or element it verifies, its measure, and its kind; a coverage statement listing the requirements no case yet reaches; and the honesty rule in force — a green run that reports its own blind spots.
cost: The discipline of writing down, next to every passing check, what it does not cover — subtracting confidence at exactly the moment the green invites it.
otherwise: Green means whatever the reader hopes: the mechanizable fraction passes, the rule is assumed to hold, and the gap between them is discovered by the failure it was hiding.
